subject: Re: Quick fit check — Redwood evaluation & demo
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@brightvelocity.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Interested in Redwood — want a short demo

Hi Ben,

I signed up for a trial on Redwood this morning and poked around the self-serve docs. We're evaluating inference platforms to replace a homegrown executor for a search-ranking feature. Quick context: BrightVelocity is an analytics platform for retail teams, we have a small model (~200M) in production for reranking and want lower latency + predictable cost.

Would love a 20–30 minute walkthrough of Redwood to see fit and ask a few ops/security questions before I loop in infra.

A few things that matter up front:
- Typical QPS: ~100 peak (bursty during reports)
- Average sequence length: 512 tokens
- We may need VPC/private deployment for compliance (SOC2 ok)

Can you propose a couple slots this week? I'm PT (PST).

Thanks,
Alex Ramos
Product Lead, BrightVelocity
alex.ramos@brightvelocity.com
[Attachment: brightvelocity-arch.png (PNG, 320KB)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@brightvelocity.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-29T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Interested in Redwood — want a short demo

Alex — great to meet you and thanks for signing up. Quick intro: I'm Ben (SDR), I handle inbound trial handoffs and help coordinate a brief demo + technical touchpoint with our solutions team. Monica (cc) is our pre-sales CS engineer and will join if we get into infra/PII/VPC details.

Before we lock a slot, could you confirm a couple quick fit questions so we tailor the demo? Short answers are totally fine:

1) Is the 100 QPS a sustained rate during business hours or concentrated spikes during report runs (seconds vs minutes)?
2) Do you need embeddings for other features, or is this solely text->rerank generation?
3) Any hard SLA / latency target (p95 target in ms)?
4) Compliance: you mentioned SOC2 — are there any additional contractual controls (data residency / logging retention / customer-managed keys)?

Proposed 20–30m slots (PST):
- Tue 11/30 10:00–10:30
- Tue 11/30 14:00–14:30
- Wed 12/01 08:30–09:00

If none work, tell me a window and I'll follow up. I'll attach a one-pager and a mutual action plan draft so we can accelerate a pilot if fit looks good.

Best,
Ben Carter
Inbound SDR — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@brightvelocity.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-30T07:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Interested in Redwood — want a short demo

Hey Ben — thanks for the quick reply and for looping Monica. Answers below:

1) Spikes: more concentrated. We run nightly/early-morning batch reports where QPS can surge over 1–2 minute windows; baseline daytime load is ~10–20 QPS.
2) Currently only rerank; we may add embeddings later for similarity features.
3) p95 target is ~120ms for the rerank call; higher during batch windows is acceptable as long as it's predictable and we can burst.
4) SOC2 is baseline. We'll need to discuss data residency for EU customers later, but for now US-hosted is fine. KMS would be nice-to-have.

Slots: Tue 11/30 14:00 PST works for me, but can we shift to 14:30 if 14:00 is tight? Also would like to include Jen Park (infra) and Marco Li (security) on the call — they're PST as well.

Thanks,
Alex
Product Lead, BrightVelocity
alex.ramos@brightvelocity.com
